classification.difficultyReason: Explain the contrast between unique cosine values on the triangle-angle domain and equal sine values for supplementary angles.

content.prompt: Explain why the cosine rule does not have an ambiguous case when solving for an unknown angle, whereas the sine rule does.

answer.short: Cosine determines one angle in $0^\circ<\theta<180^\circ$. Sine can give two supplementary angles, which coincide at $90^\circ$.
answer.worked: For $0^\circ<\theta<180^\circ$, each cosine value corresponds to exactly one angle. However, $\sin\theta=\sin(180^\circ-\theta)$, so the sine rule can give two distinct supplementary angles. At $\theta=90^\circ$, these angles coincide.
